newsitem.title: CHINA: China Construction Bank sets credit card link.
newsitem.headline: China Construction Bank sets credit card link.

text.p: China Construction Bank said it had reached an agreement with a Chinese travel and merchant group in a joint programme that would expand its credit card operations.
The major state-run bank would cooperate with the China Intec Group to issue a combined credit and discount card next month, bank officials told reporters.

The new card, to be issued early next year, would allow Construction Bank customers to make purchases on credit and obtain discounts at some 500 hotels and shops around the country that participate in the China Intec network.

China has been moving towards greater use of credit cards to reduce the reliance on cash in the financial system though the central bank has been concerned about fraud and the possible impact on inflation.
Chinese banks have seen a much faster growth in their debit card business than in that of Western-style credit cards.

The Construction Bank has about 8 million customers using its "Dragon" bank card but most are debit card holders who must first deposit cash in a bank account before they can use the card to spend those funds, said Zhou Zhenhai, head of the bank's Beijing operations.
"This will be a real credit card," Zhou told reporters.
Unlike credit cards elsewhere, a guarantor is required for a credit card in China.

Zhou said that the central bank had approved the new card and that limits on spending would mean there would be little or no impact on inflation. He did not give details of the limits, saying they would vary according to customer creditworthiness.
